blocks.text: The sweeping conclusion that Joshua took the land and its kings “at one time” should be read alongside the book’s later notices that land and peoples still remained and that possession was incomplete. The chapter’s summary is therefore not necessarily a claim that every part of the land had already been fully occupied.

Across the wider conquest narratives, archaeological evidence from sites such as Jericho, Ai, Hazor, the highlands, and Mount Ebal varies by site and chronology; it does not produce one uncontested reconstruction of the conquest. The warfare and herem passages also require historical, literary, ethical, and theological scrutiny and cannot be used to authorize modern territorial or religious violence.

sections.title: Questions Raised by the Wider Conquest Account
